questions.stem: The thermostat in an engine cooling system:
options: Filters sea water before the pump
Pumps the coolant round the engine
Regulates coolant temperature
Removes air from the fuel lines
questions.explanation: A stuck thermostat is a classic cause of overheating.

questions.stem: The expansion tank is placed at the highest point in a fresh water cooling system so it can:
options: Act as a sump for leaking coolant
Hold a reserve of spare fuel close to the engine
Cool the exhaust before it leaves
Allow for expansion and let air escape
questions.explanation: It keeps the system full and helps release trapped air.

questions.stem: A sea water strainer in a cooling circuit is there to:
options: Reduce engine noise from the water pump
Warm the water before it enters the engine
Add coolant automatically when the level drops
Stop debris from blocking the coolers and pump
questions.explanation: A blocked strainer is a common cause of overheating. Clean it regularly.

questions.stem: Sea water is not used to cool the inside of a diesel engine mainly because it:
options: Is too cold for the engine block
Lacks the pressure to circulate well
Causes corrosion and scale and deposits salt
Boils at a lower temperature than fresh water
questions.explanation: Fresh water with additives is used inside the engine.

questions.stem: You should not remove a hot pressure cap from an expansion tank because:
options: The thermostat will close and stay shut
The cap seal will be damaged if opened warm
The coolant can flash to steam and scald you
The engine will stall from the pressure drop
questions.explanation: Let the system cool and open the cap slowly with a cloth over it.

questions.stem: A failed raw water impeller will most likely cause:
options: Low oil pressure at normal running speed
A flat battery from the extra electrical load
Black smoke only, with normal temperatures
Overheating because the sea water flow stops
questions.explanation: Check the water flow at the exhaust. Carry a spare impeller.

questions.stem: In a fresh water and sea water heat exchanger, the fresh water side is usually kept at the higher pressure so that a leak:
options: Loses a little coolant but does not let salt into the engine
Lets salt water into the engine, where it is easier to detect
Stops the circulating pump so the alarm warns the crew
Heats the sea water side so the cooler works harder
questions.explanation: Pressure order is arranged so a leak does the least harm.

questions.stem: A keel cooler cools the engine fresh water by:
options: Running it through pipes fixed to the outside of the hull
Spraying it with cold fuel from the day tank as it passes
Pumping it through the bilge so the bilge water cools it
Drawing sea water through the engine block and head
questions.explanation: It needs no raw water intake, so there is less fouling inside.
